gen-dafont-origami-lora: Lora brings a classic serif body with a broad-mouthed c and only a faint hairline thinning. Origami sits above it as a single-stroke brush heading, its lowercase packed dense like poured lead type; a roughly two-to-one jump in size helps the heading hold its ground.
gen-dafont-origami-noto-serif: Contemporary and a bit odd, Origami draws curves and straights at one constant width, like a brush dragged steadily. Noto Serif, a classic serif with a prominent x-height, does the opposite job, letting a subtle pen-like modulation carry the paragraphs.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-fs-gambetta: Outrun Future traces a constant-width outline you could follow with a finger, its letters holding a wide distance apart. Gambetta, a text serif, comes in beneath with channels flowing into each counter and a stroke that shifts noticeably but never dramatically.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-lora: Outrun Future has synthwave authority, every stroke the same gauge. Lora, a classic serif, then carries the reading with a pen-like swell in its bowls and a welcoming c, so paragraphs move along with a bookish, unhurried feel.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-noto-serif: Outrun Future holds every bowl without any swelling, its tall outlines spaced wide and its ascenders short. And Noto Serif, a classic serif, answers underneath with strokes that vary in weight, though never by much, and a prominent x-height.
gen-dafont-over-there-crimson-pro: Crimson Pro reads refined and tightly packed, its open shapes carrying a subtle thick and thin cadence through each line. And Over There stamps the heading like toothpaste squeezed in one steady line, leaving generous white space between its glyphs.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-neco: Vintage-military swagger, drawn as if by a fixed-width nib with plenty of white space between the glyphs. Over There leads with that command; Neco, a classic serif, follows with a measured swell and curves that never pinch shut.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-recia: Recia is a classic serif with sharp authority, its modulation visible mainly up close and its openings generous. Recia gives the bent-paperclip lines of Over There, which have no swelling at all, a measured swell from hairline to stem to lean against.
gen-dafont-over-there-newsreader: Over There looks drawn by a fixed-width nib, with no stress tilting its round letters. It excels at commanding vintage-military headings, while Newsreader, a serif with open jaws on every curve, excels at gently modulated, refined text.
gen-dafont-over-there-source-serif-4: Lines like bent rope or tubing, spaced with plenty of white space, make Over There instantly recognizable as vintage-military. Source Serif 4 supplies dignified, gently tilted verticals against them.
